Every day, people come to Facebook and Instagram to share their stories, see
the world through the eyes of others and connect with friends and causes. The
conversations that happen on Facebook reflect the diversity of a community of
more than two billion people communicating across countries and cultures and
in dozens of languages. We recognize how important it is for Facebook to be a
place where people feel empowered to communicate, and we take our role in
keeping abuse off our service seriously. That's why we have developed a set
of Community Standards, which govern the content that people are allowed
to share on our platforms, with the goal to encourage expression and create a
safe environment.
Background: Facebook works with trusted partner organizations who are
familiar with our policies to provide critical insights and on-the-ground
context to aid in our content moderation. We work with over 400 trusted
partners in 113 countries around the globe.
The goal of the Trusted Partner program is to establish and maintain
relationships and reporting channels with expert organizations that raise

queries and concerns about problematic content on Facebook and Instagram
to:
• address harmful content trends and prevent harm,
• foster online safety and security, and
• inform the development of fair and transparent policies.
Our partners are non-governmental organizations, human rights defenders,
humanitarian organizations, activists, or researchers that enable us to:
• learn from on-the-ground actors across the globe, especially those
representing marginalized communities,
• identify and address policy, process, or training gaps to improve the
standard report review process, and
• ensure our review of high-priority content and accounts is informed by
critical and up-to-date context.
Reporting: Our Trusted Partner Channel provides our partner organizations
with an expedited way of reporting this content to Facebook. The channel is
staffed 24/7 by a team of escalations specialists who triage reports and route
them to expert teams for analysis. Once a report is received, our team will
review the content against our Community Standards and if necessary, seek
additional context from the Trusted Partner. We will then respond back to the
Trusted Partner with our assessment. Trusted Partners are under no obligation
to report to Facebook. When Trusted Partners do report, we will only remove
the content and accounts that are in violation of our Community Standards.
Confidentiality: Given the challenging environments many of our partner
organizations work in, we keep all Trusted Partners and their reporting
practices confidential. However, partner organizations should feel free to share
the nature of our relationship and their reporting practices however they'd like.
Policy Consultations: Our team, which manages the Trusted Partner program
sits within Facebook's Content Policy team, the group that creates our
Community Standards. In the process of developing / revising our policies, we
seek input from a broad spectrum of experts and users including academics,
journalists, human rights defenders, and civil society organizations. When we
are working to develop a policy that relates to our Trusted Partner's work or
community, we reach out to see if you would be willing to discuss the subject
with us over a video conference or phone call. The feedback we receive during
these calls informs the development of fair and transparent policies that help
make our platform safer and advance freedom of expression for our users.
-
Johnny Walsh

Deputy Assistant Administrator for Democracy, Human Rights, and
Governance
U.S. Agency for International Development
